transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Hassan, thank you for meeting with me. I have some important information to share with you regarding your medications.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can tell by your face this isn't good news. Just tell me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to be direct with you. There has been a medical error. A medication that was supposed to be stopped three days ago was not discontinued because the pharmacy was never notified. I am very sorry. This was our mistake, and I take full responsibility for it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Which one?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was the Gabapentin. It was marked as stopped in your electronic notes, but that instruction didn't make it to the pharmacy, so you continued taking it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Well, I've been feeling a bit more groggy, but my pain has been flared up anyway. This is just how this illness goes, isn't it? It's a rollercoaster.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a very difficult road, and I know you've dealt with a lot of setbacks. But the grogginess you're feeling is a direct result of the medication staying in your system when it should have been gone.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know. I've had bad reactions before. Maybe my body is just reacting poorly to the flare.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see why you'd think that, given everything you've been through. But in this specific case, the cause was the error we made with the pharmacy.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's always something. Another mistake, another "sorry." I'm just tired of being the one who has to deal with the fallout of someone forgetting to click a button.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: This is a heavy thing to hear, and it's completely unfair that you're the one bearing the burden of our mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Exactly. So what now? Do I just stop taking it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, you must stop taking the Gabapentin immediately.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep an eye on you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's it? You're just going to "keep an eye" on me? After you've spent three days giving me a drug I didn't need?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to make sure you're safe.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Safe. Right. I've heard that one before. What is the actual plan to make sure I don't end up like this again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll make sure the charts are updated.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's vague. Who is doing what? When am I going to know if this has caused any long-term issue with my kidney function or whatever else this stuff does?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just monitor the labs.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Tomorrow? Next week?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Whenever the next scheduled draw is.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're not really giving me much to go on here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry, I just want to make sure we're focused on the immediate stop of the drug first.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I've stopped it. Now I want to know why this keeps happening in this building.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it's incredibly frustrating to feel like a passenger in your own care. I am truly sorry that we let you down.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I've had three adverse events in two years. You guys always apologize, but the pharmacy still misses things.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize that an apology doesn't undo the fact that you've been taking a medication you shouldn't have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It doesn't. It just makes me feel like I have to double-check every single pill I take.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is a completely reasonable way to feel. You shouldn't have to be the one auditing your care.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So, are you going to tell me exactly what the next step is or not?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just see how you feel over the next few days.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll make a note to check back in.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is exactly what I mean. You're sorry, but you've got nothing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you. I really do. I am sorry that I don't have a more detailed timeline for you right this second.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Typical.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a lot to process. I'm going to stay here with you as long as you need to talk through how you're feeling about this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm feeling like I can't trust you people.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is a very honest and very fair reaction given the circumstances.

H.justification: The resident remains calm and regulated under significant pushback, never interrupts the patient, and avoids rushing language.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly and in lay language, but the resident never performed a comprehension check.

A.justification: The resident used direct apology language, took full responsibility ('our mistake'), and maintained this accountability throughout the patient's anger.

R.justification: The resident named specific emotions ('frustrating', 'heavy', 'unfair') and engaged with the patient's shared history of adverse events.

T.justification: The resident provided only placeholders and vague responses ('we'll just monitor', 'soon', 'whenever the next scheduled draw is') without specific timelines or a prevention plan.
